relays.notes: PRIMARY on the strongest evidence available: the only relay that answered goodearth-mcp from Horizon on 2026-09-02 while four others returned 403, 502, 503 and a timeout. Accepts kind-30078 and serves it back. An operator runs in a datacenter, so datacenter reachability is the measurement that counts.

Accepted a kind-30078 write and served it back, measured 2026-09-02 from a residential IP. Behaviour from an operator's datacenter is UNVERIFIED — ranked above the relays known to refuse datacenters, below the one known to accept them.

caveat: Relays must both accept writes and serve reads, and reachability is measured FROM SOMEWHERE. Cloudflare-fronted relays serve residential IPs and refuse datacenter ones: on 2026-09-02, relay.0xchat.com returned 403 and relay.damus.io 503 to an operator on Horizon while both answered a laptop normally. Rank on what operators actually observe, not on what a workstation can reach.
order_policy: This list ORDERS relays; it never eliminates them. No relay is perfect, so a policy that removes the imperfect ones converges on an empty list and an operator with nowhere to read its credentials. Operators report the relays that failed them (the Oracle's report_relay_failure); the most-flagged sink toward the bottom and the dependable rise. Rank is a measurement and changes freely. Membership is a commitment and only grows — a relay leaves only when the federation agrees nothing of ours can still be sitting on it.
